text:
alex_people_ops: Quick heads-up — SF hub is launching a 6-week pilot starting Mon 2026-05-04 for 'Quiet Floor' desk-hotel and visitor flow changes. Goal: reduce noise on the top floor, test phone-booth distribution, and validate a new desk booking cadence. Summary below and TL;DR at the top.

alex_people_ops: TL;DR: top floor (4th) becomes Quiet Zone 9am–4pm weekdays; phone booths get reserved + 3 new booths; desk hoteling moves from ad-hoc to 48h prebook window; visitor check-in moves to kiosk by the lobby; Deep-clean Sundays once during pilot. No mass closures expected. :loud_sound::no_entry:  

jamie_facilities: Quick note — elevator #2 will have short maintenance windows Tuesday evening (20:00–22:00) during setup. If you need freight access, DM me.

sarah_eng: Thanks — does Quiet Zone apply to meetings on that floor?

alex_people_ops: Good q. Quiet Zone means: individual desks are phone-free and low-volume; small huddle rooms on 4th can still be booked but please use headset/mute and keep calls in meeting rooms where possible. We’ll add signage and a short etiquette card.

matt_design: How do we book desks now? The old link sometimes double-books.

alex_people_ops: New booking flow: please use the internal booking app (https://intra.redwood.company/desks). Rules for pilot: 48h prebook window, max 4 consecutive days per person, cancel at least 2h before to free the slot. We'll monitor metrics.

lia_hybrid: Will commuter parking/subsidy be affected for days when offices are quieter? My team splits days and sometimes drives on short notice.

alex_people_ops: No changes to commuter stipend during the pilot. If trends show underutilized parking we may run a discounted visitor/contractor parking pool later, but any stipend changes would be communicated well in advance.

jamie_facilities: facilities-bot posted: "ELEVATOR #2: scheduled maintenance Tue 2026-05-05 20:00–22:00 — expect brief service interruptions."

sarah_eng: Any plan for folks who need a phone booth for an interview that falls inside Quiet Zone hours?

alex_people_ops: We will reserve 1 booth as 'On-Demand Interview' via the booking app for panel interviews. If you need it, mark as "Interview" when booking and ops will prioritize.

matt_design: Will there be signage and a simple FAQ?

alex_people_ops: Yes — signage, a FAQ doc (link below), and a short drop-in Q&A with People Ops + Facilities next Fri 11am in the mezz lounge. FAQ: https://intra.redwood.company/ops/sf-quiet-pilot.

lia_hybrid: Appreciate the heads up. Any changes for vendors or contractors dropping by?

jamie_facilities: Contractors will check in at the new kiosk. Vendor badges will be time-limited and escorts required in the pilot.

sarah_eng: Will there be quiet hours enforced with warnings or just signage?

alex_people_ops: First phase is sign + gentle reminders from floor hosts. If problems persist we'll switch to automated reminders via the booking app and escalate to managers.

matt_design: :thumbsup: when does the 6-week pilot end?

alex_people_ops: Pilot end date: Sun 2026-06-14. We'll run a short survey at weeks 2 and 6 and publish utilization + sentiment metrics.

lia_hybrid: Can we opt out if someone needs to be on-call and needs a headset area?

alex_people_ops: On-call exceptions are fine — pick a different floor or use reserved interview booth. If you have recurring on-call needs, DM me and we’ll carve out a recurring slot.

jamie_facilities: facilities-bot posted: "DEEP-CLEAN: Sunday 2026-05-10 scheduled; please clear desk surfaces Friday evening if you use shared desks that week."

sarah_eng: Thanks, bookmarking the FAQ.

alex_people_ops: Thanks all. If you have accessibility or accommodation needs related to the pilot please reply here or email people-ops@redwood.ai. We want this to be inclusive. :heart:
